Two maps and their composites

Elements of Aff(1, ℝ) as lines y = sign·scale·x + add; the composites X∘Y and Y∘X, and where they differ. A picture shows a structure; it is not evidence that the structure means anything beyond its definition.

X Y X∘Y (Y first) Y∘X
About this visual

What you are looking at. Two elements X and Y of Aff(1, ℝ), each a map x ↦ sign·scale·x + add, drawn as straight lines y = f(x) on the plane. A third and fourth line are the two composites X∘Y (Y fires first) and Y∘X. The dashed diagonal is y = x; where a line crosses it is that map's fixed point.

How to read it. Set add, ln scale and the sign of X and of Y. Watch the red and gold lines: they coincide exactly when X and Y commute. Move the start point x₀: the cobweb on the diagonal follows x₀ → Y(x₀) → X(Y(x₀)).

What it shows. That composition of two lines is a line (the group is closed), that its slope is the product of the slopes (scale × scale, sign × sign) and that its intercept is addX + signX·scaleX·addY, so the order of two maps differs only in the intercept unless the maps share a fixed point or one is a pure sign or scale of the other.

What it does not show. Anything about the engine's own arithmetic beyond one float: the numbers here are floats, and the exact (Fraction) statements are on the grid page. It does not show the record of steps: composing keeps only the resulting line.

Numbers to check. X∘Y has add = aX + gXsXaY, scale = sXsY, sign = gXgY. With X = ADD(3) and Y = SCALE(2): X∘Y = (3, 2, +1), Y∘X = (6, 2, +1).

running self-check…

Code and data. Everything shown is recomputed in the browser by ass.js (composition, inverse, commutator, word, fold, the Long Path and exact rational arithmetic) and compared with the numbers the Python engine produced (ass_data.js); the result is printed above. Light and dark follow the system.

Literature and documentation.

  • Wikipedia, "Affine group": Aff(1, ℝ) = ℝ ⋊ ℝ*, the group of x ↦ ax + b.
  • Wikipedia, "Semidirect product".
  • Wikipedia, "Commutator": the group commutator [x, y] = x⁻¹y⁻¹xy used here.
  • Wikipedia, "Smith chart" and "Reflection coefficient": Γ = tanh(u/2) is the real-axis form of the fold.
  • S. Lang, Algebra (Springer GTM 211), chapter on groups: semidirect products and the affine group.
  • N. J. A. Sloane, OEIS A005132: Recamán's sequence, the set-membership flip test that ASSWord.would_collide copies.
